observation.visible_scene: A close-up on a tan wooden tabletop against a dark, out-of-focus background shows a white foam object. The object consists of a solid rectangular block on the left joined to a row of vertical, wavy/zigzag walls on the right. A metal knife blade enters the frame from the top and is angled into the left portion of the foam, near the junction of the block and the wavy walls.
visible_changes: For the first ~1 s the knife blade remains angled into the foam's left region with only small positional shifts, and the wavy walls stand nearly upright.
Beginning around t≈1 s and continuing to the end, the wavy/zigzag wall section progressively tilts and leans to the right, rotating about its base from an upright pose to a clear diagonal slant.
The solid rectangular block on the left stays largely in place on the table throughout the clip.

As the foam leans, the visible part of the knife blade shifts downward within the foam and then recedes toward the upper-left, becoming mostly out of frame by the last frames while the foam tilts away from it.
The dark opening/hole in the middle of the wavy walls translates and changes apparent shape as the wall section tilts.
The cast shadow on the right side of the table shifts slightly, consistent with the foam's changing orientation.
outside_clip_unknowns: What precedes the blade's insertion and whether the foam is being cut, levered, or pushed is not shown.
Whether the leaning foam ultimately falls, snaps, or stays standing beyond the last frame is unknown.
The presence or motion of any operator holding the knife is outside the visible frame.
uncertain_details: It is not fully determinable from the frames whether the blade actively moves or is simply occluded by the tilting foam; relative blade-foam position clearly changes.
Possible small camera jitter cannot be separated from the foam's motion; the background appears mostly static but is not a reliable reference.
The exact contact point and mechanism between blade and foam are not visually resolved.
